purpose: Stage 10 of a badminton CV system that determines point winners from rally footage. The module attributes the striker (wrist-anchored in body-height units), fits an alternation rhythm to assign court halves to strokes, filters landing positions kinematically (settle cap + carry filter), and outputs a verdict (won/lost) using winner-serves-next with landing geometry as fallback.

public_api.name: Half
public_api.role: StrEnum denoting court half (Top/Bot) for spatial reasoning throughout the module

public_api.name: Verdict
public_api.role: StrEnum for rally outcome (won/lost) relative to the striker

public_api.name: VerdictSource
public_api.role: StrEnum labeling where a verdict came from (next_server, landing_geometry, or net_rule)

public_api.name: project_pixels_to_court
public_api.role: Convert (2, N) pixel coords at given resolution to normalised court coords using homography

public_api.name: attribute_half
public_api.role: Determine court half of the sticky-tracked nearest player to the shuttle at a frame

public_api.name: fit_alternation
public_api.role: Score two possible alternating phases to find the fitted final-stroke half from per-stroke guesses

public_api.name: next_server_half
public_api.role: Derive winner half per rally from winner-serves-next: rally n's winner is rally n+1's fitted first-stroke half

public_api.name: LandingWindow
public_api.role: NamedTuple holding the safe landing search endpoint and the boundary conditions that closed it

public_api.name: landing_window
public_api.role: Find safe landing endpoint by scanning forward from contact frame, handling lob re-entry and sustained loss

public_api.name: window_end
public_api.role: Convenience wrapper returning just the end_frame from landing_window

public_api.name: LandingKinematics
public_api.role: NamedTuple of per-frame kinematic signals: shuttle-to-wrist ratio, shuttle-to-ankle ratio, and speed

public_api.name: LandingFilterOptions
public_api.role: NamedTuple of tunable landing filter parameters (settle window/threshold, carry window/threshold, ankle rule toggle)

public_api.name: convert_landing_options
public_api.role: Convert landing options from base-30 FPS to the actual video FPS

public_api.name: build_landing_kinematics
public_api.role: Compute per-frame carry/ankle proximity ratios (body-height units) and shuttle speed for the filter

public_api.name: filtered_descending_landing
public_api.role: Find the landing: last descending (increasing image-y) run surviving settle cap and carry filter

public_api.name: is_net_ender
public_api.role: Test whether the rally flight never crossed the net line and died in the net band (implies strike lost)

public_api.name: inout_verdict
public_api.role: Determine won/lost/None for a landing vs receiver's singles half with margin tolerance M

public_api.name: LandingMargins
public_api.role: NamedTuple of signed clearances: overall margin_m, net distance, sideline/baseline distance

public_api.name: landing_margins
public_api.role: Calculate signed court-metre clearances from a landing to the receiver's singles half boundaries

public_api.name: corner_error_band_from_corners
public_api.role: Propagate homography corner-marking error to court metres via 16 corner perturbations

public_api.name: corner_error_band_m
public_api.role: Query homography corner positions for a video and compute the corner error band

public_api.name: Landing
public_api.role: NamedTuple of one rally's picked landing: frame, normalised court position, court half, border flag, net_ender flag

public_api.name: pick_landing_to_end
public_api.role: Apply kinematic filtering and project a picked landing from pixels to normalised court coords

public_api.name: geometric_verdict
public_api.role: Verdict and winner half from landing geometry alone (net rule or in/out with best_guess fallback)

public_api.name: VerdictRow
public_api.role: NamedTuple of one rally's verdict for output: rally_id, striker_half, verdict, source, margin, band flags

public_api.name: GeometricVerdictRow
public_api.role: NamedTuple for diagnostic consistency check: rally_id, geometric verdict/winner, agreement with verdict

public_api.name: rally_verdict
public_api.role: Assemble one rally's VerdictRow: next-server call if available, else geometric best-guess fallback

public_api.name: hit_height
public_api.role: ShuttleSet hit_height coding (1=above net-band centre, 2=at/below) for a contact frame

public_api.name: HitHeightRow
public_api.role: NamedTuple of one stroke's hit_height: rally_id, stroke_idx, contact_frame, coded height

public_api.name: build_hit_height_rows
public_api.role: Convert flat list of (rally_id, stroke_idx, contact_frame) tuples to HitHeightRow list

stumbles.quote:
return [final_half if (last - i) % 2 == 0 else OTHER_HALF[final_half]
        for i in range(n_strokes)]
stumbles.why_unclear: The list comprehension creates an alternating pattern by working backwards from the final stroke (last = n_strokes - 1) using modulo to flip halves. The backwards indexing and why this produces the correct forward-order alternation requires mental simulation to verify.

stumbles.quote:
reason_order = ('next_rally', 'definitive_exclusion', 'sustained_loss', 'video_end')
reasons = tuple(
    reason for reason in reason_order
    if boundaries.get(reason) == safe_end
)
stumbles.why_unclear: The code collects reasons matching safe_end in a specific order, implying multiple boundary conditions could reach the same endpoint. The docstring says 'all guards tied at that endpoint' but it's not immediately obvious from reading landing_window why this can occur or what the precedence order means.

This reordering converts corner coordinates from 'source order' to TL, TR, BR, BL order (stated in the docstring above), but the module does not import or define what source_order contains or what get_corner_camera returns, so the rationale for this specific permutation cannot be verified inside the file alone.
